text:
alex: Quick q — what's the recommended client behavior for handling 429 vs 5xx in streaming + auth-refresh flows? Specifically trying to finalize guidance for Rust/Go SDK READMEs.

maya: TL;DR: 1) honor Retry-After if present; 2) exponential backoff with full jitter for 429/5xx; 3) for non-idempotent operations only auto-retry if an `Idempotency-Key` was provided; 4) for streams prefer resume tokens instead of re-sending entire payload.

sam: Adding: watch out for token-refresh races. If many requests get 401 and all try to refresh, backend sees a flood -> 429s. Use a singleflight/coalescing refresh so only one refresh in flight, others wait for the new token.

rachel: Language notes: Rust SDK — make reconnection Future cancel-safe and keep KV-cache pointer separate so resuming doesn't leak memory. Go — use context cancellation and backoff in a goroutine, prefer math/rand for jitter. Python — async clients: await token refresh before re-opening stream to avoid duplicate in-flight refreshes.

alex: Good points. For a long-lived stream that returns 5xx mid-stream, should clients: a) reconnect and re-send full prompt, b) reconnect and use resume token if server provides, or c) propagate error to app? What's our recommended order?

maya: Preferred order: 1) resume token (if present) — best, minimal work; 2) if no resume token, and the operation is idempotent or has an `Idempotency-Key`, re-send with the same idempotency key; 3) otherwise surface error to app (don't auto-retry non-idempotent). Make sure to surface a clear enum to the app: StreamState::Partial / Retrying / Failed so UI can decide.

sam: Example singleflight-ish pseudocode for token refresh (Rust/Go pseudo):
```
if resp.status == 401 {
  let token = await token_manager.refresh_once().await; // singleflight guarantee
  retry_with(token)
}
```
And for 429/5xx backoff: exponential base 200ms, max 30s, full jitter randomized each attempt.

rachel: Also allow SDK users to opt into aggressive vs conservative backoff presets. Add two presets: `backoff::presets::conservative` (start 500ms, max 60s) and `backoff::presets::aggressive` (start 100ms, max 10s) — useful for low-latency product teams.

ops-bot: heads-up: we saw a spike of 429s in eu-west last night due to autoscaler lag (2026-11-03 02:12 UTC). Temporary mitigation: enabled burst capacity and queued some requests. If you rely on auto-retry for UX, prefer resume tokens + idempotency keys while we tune. :warning:

alex: Sounds good. I'll draft an SDK README section that covers: honor Retry-After, backoff presets, resume token flow, idempotency-key guidance, and token refresh singleflight. Can someone GH-review? @maya @sam @rachel ? :thumbsup:

maya: happy to review — ping the PR.

sam: I can too, especially the token-refresh bits.

rachel: I'll look at language examples (Rust + Go). Suggest we include small snippets and a flow chart.

alex: awesome — I'll open PR with the draft + examples and link to internal docs <https://internal.redwood.dev/sdk/retries>.
